evidence.evidence_text: Multilingual large language models (LLMs) face an often-overlooked challenge stemming from intrinsic semantic differences across languages.

Through examining responses of conversational multilingual AIs in English and Japanese with the cases used in philosophy (cases of knowledge-how attributions), this study demonstrates that even state-of-the-art LLMs provide divergent and internally inconsistent responses.

Multilingual large language models (LLMs) face an often-overlooked challenge stemming from intrinsic semantic differences across languages.
Linguistic divergence can sometimes lead to cross-linguistic disagreements--disagreements purely due to semantic differences about a relevant concept.
